questions.q: What is an Azure storage account?
options: The top-level container and billing/management boundary for Azure storage services
A single file stored in the cloud
A type of virtual machine
A billing plan for Azure Databricks only
questions.explain: Everything else in this chapter — blobs, containers, ADLS Gen2 — lives underneath one storage account.

questions.q: Which five storage services can live under a single storage account?
options: Blob storage, Azure Files, Queues, Tables, and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
Only Blob storage and nothing else
Virtual machines, databases, and networks
Only Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
questions.explain: One account is a single namespace and billing boundary spanning all five of these services.

questions.q: Which account kind supports all five storage services, including the hierarchical namespace needed for ADLS Gen2?
options: StorageV2 (general purpose v2)
Premium Files only
Classic storage
Table storage exclusively
questions.explain: StorageV2 is the account kind used throughout this course's labs.

questions.q: What does the redundancy setting (LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS) control?
options: How many copies of your data Azure keeps, and where those copies are located
How fast the storage account can process requests
Which programming languages can connect to the account
The maximum file size that can be stored
questions.explain: More redundancy (spreading copies across zones or regions) means more protection against outages, at higher cost.

questions.q: What dataset does this entire 62-lesson course use for its hands-on labs?
options: The real, public NYC Taxi & Limousine Commission (TLC) Trip Record Data
A private dataset only available to Azure enterprise customers
Randomly generated data with no real-world structure
AdventureWorks2012, the same database used in the T-SQL course
questions.explain: NYC TLC trip data is real, public, and widely used across the industry for exactly this kind of data engineering training.
